title: Linux Super Timeline Creation and Analysis
learning_objectives: Spot what is normal on a Linux host.
Turn findings into a clean response plan.

post_assessment.question: Which artifact is best for quick Linux triage?
What is the main goal of live response?
What should you do first with a suspicious host?

content_blocks.text: Start with calm. Speed matters, panic destroys evidence.
Live response is about making fast decisions without trampling the machine.
Think of the computer like a bedroom after a break-in. Look first, touch less.
Run a safe triage command set and note what changed before and after.
A weird SSH login at 3 AM usually has a trail in auth logs, shell history, and running processes.
Three questions: who touched it, what changed, what is still alive?
Write the one thing you would collect first if you had only 5 minutes.
Good DFIR is disciplined curiosity, not heroics.
